calibration.rule: MEASURED AND LEFT ALONE. The same per-species temperature fit that moved morel's floors was run on chanterelle and every candidate lost. Do not 'improve' these numbers without re-running cmd/validate-backtest -fit-temp; they have already beaten their data-derived replacements.
calibration.evidence: n=350 observations, 5-fold cross-validated grouped by observation, paired DeLong. Floors at the observed p5 (35->38 air, 40->38 soil): effort-matched AUC 0.795 -> 0.786, -0.0092 +/- 0.0030, RESOLVED WORSE; ring undecided. All five parameters at p5/p50/p95: ring -0.0159 +/- 0.0051 and effort-matched -0.0235 +/- 0.0048, both resolved worse. The 1,296-member grid search, cross-validated, also lost effort-matched (-0.0159 +/- 0.0034). Floor sensitivity is monotone: the further the floors drop below their current 35/40, the worse it gets, reaching -0.078 effort-matched at p30. Only 1% of real chanterelle fruitings sit below the 35F air floor and 11% below the 40F soil floor, against 25% and 62% for morel. Every figure here survives a cluster bootstrap over whole observations: the clustered standard error matches DeLong's paired one to the fourth decimal on all three control sets, so the rejection is not an artefact of treating correlated records as independent.
calibration.caveat: This is why the global 10F temperature shoulder was the wrong shape rather than the wrong idea: it helped morel (+0.101) and cost chanterelle (-0.011) because chanterelle's floors were already close to right and morel's were not. A negative result on this species is what makes the morel result a calibration finding instead of a tuning constant.
calibration.reproduce: go run ./cmd/validate-backtest -species chanterelle -sweep -n 350 -spatial 2 -target-group 2 -background 2 -compare "air-min=38,soil-min=38"   # the p5 floors this species rejected. Add -fit-temp to re-derive from scratch.

season.notes: Parasitic fungus colonizing Russula and Lactarius hosts. Fruits on a 3-7 day lag after its host; the host itself has a shorter rain lag (1-3 days). Often partially buried.

hypomyces_lactifluorum.special_notes: Two-organism model, now implemented: score = host_probability * parasite_probability (internal/species/host.go). The host is a MUSHROOM, not a tree -- Hypomyces lactifluorum parasitises a Russula brevipes (and some Lactarius) fruitbody -- so the host term is that host profile's own ScoreSite score read off the same daily weather series truncated to the lag day, taken as the maximum over the 3-7 day lag window. The parasite term keeps its own temperature gate and delegates MOISTURE entirely to the host: a lobster's water comes from the fruitbody it is consuming, not from the day's rain, which is why the wet-up -> incubation timeline made this species worse (67% -> 84% false negatives) when it was applied to the parasite instead of to the host. DATA FIX: `association` used to read hemlock/spruce/fir/oak/beech. Those are the trees the HOST associates with, one level too high, and a uniform reader of `association` (terrain.TreeCoverResult.HostScore) would have scored a lobster for standing next to an oak. The list moved to species/russula_brevipes.json, where it belongs; this species associates with no tree directly, and gets its forest requirement through its host, which is mycorrhizal and carries the forest habitat gate itself. Temp floors recalibrated 2026-09 to fall-fruiting reality (host-tracking); previous summer floors (55F/55F) blanked legitimate cool-fall finds. PUBLICATION STATUS, MEASURED 2026-09-08: RANKABLE BUT NOT ANSWERABLE. Across the real PNW records that could be scored, the HIGHEST score any lobster observation reached is 0.195, and the share firing at the 0.25 threshold is 0% -- a 100% false-negative rate not because the model is blind but because the whole score distribution sits below the band floors. Effort-matched AUC is 0.781 +/- 0.042, so the ordering is real: lobster pixels can be ranked against each other. What cannot happen is a lobster pixel entering a published band, because none ever will. A lobster map can therefore say 'better here than there' and must not say 'go here'; publishing it as a foraging map would be indefensible. Fixing this means recalibrating the parasite term's absolute level against its own observations, not lowering the band thresholds to meet it.

calibration.rule: each fitted floor placed at the 5th percentile of this species' own observed temperatures, as the gate sees them (lapse-corrected 3-day trailing mean). No search: the grid search over 1,188 parameter sets generalised WORSE (+0.042 ring vs +0.092 for this rule), which is the freedom talking.
calibration.evidence: n=350 observations, 5-fold cross-validated grouped by observation, paired DeLong, with the delta ALSO bootstrapped over whole observations carrying their own controls (clustering did not widen it: 0.0081 against DeLong's 0.0082 on the ring). Ring AUC 0.700 -> 0.792 (+0.0917 +/- 0.0082); effort-matched (target-group) 0.589 -> 0.666 (+0.0775 +/- 0.0243); both RESOLVED better and agreeing in sign and magnitude, which is the test the habitat ramp failed when it turned out to be reading road access. Temporal (the fit objective) +0.0083 +/- 0.0041, significant but under the 80%-power floor. False negatives 67% -> 32%. Reverting the two floors together costs far more than the sum of reverting them one at a time (-0.092 ring jointly against -0.010 and -0.030 singly): below BOTH floors both bells read zero, so the two numbers are not independent and were measured as a pair.
calibration.caveat: The effort-matched control set held only 17 points when this was measured -- Open-Meteo's daily quota ran out before it could be filled -- so that row is the weakest of the three despite being resolved. Re-run with a full target-group set before quoting it as the headline. Lowering soil_temp_min_f also moves the SOIL BELL'S MIDPOINT from 60F to 56F, because the bell's peak is (min+max)/2; that is a real second change and it was measured as part of this one, not separately. A 10F cold shoulder on TOP of these floors still measures +0.013 +/- 0.004 ring and is deliberately not shipped -- see TempShoulderF.
calibration.reproduce: go run ./cmd/validate-backtest -species morel -sweep -n 350 -spatial 2 -target-group 2 -background 2 -compare "air-min=45,soil-min=50"   # the old floors, measured against the new ones on the same points. Add -fit-temp to re-derive from scratch.

season.notes: Spring specialist. Loves disturbed ground — recent burns, landscaping, river bottoms. Often fruits along riparian corridors and in orchards. The field-guide rule of thumb is "sustained 50°F+ soil at 4 inches", and that number used to be copied straight into soil_temp_min_f — where it cut off 62% of real PNW fruitings, because the model compares against a lapse-corrected 3-day mean of the 0-7cm ERA5 layer, which is not a 4-inch spot reading on a warm afternoon. The floors are now derived from this species' own observed p5; see calibration below.

Choice edible with firm white flesh; safe boletes here have white-to-yellow pores that do not stain intensely blue and a mild taste. Fruiting is tied to SNOWMELT moisture more than to discrete rain events, so the precip and days-after-rain fields are weak predictors here — flagged lower-confidence, and elevation band matters more than rainfall for this species.
